assertion.statement: On the stated characteristic-zero nonquadratic tests, restriction to the exact common kernel is injective and two independent evaluated classes admit one rank-two localization. Finite-stage Chebotarev realizes it with exact inner-limit basis-cochain matrix equality before minimal-model denominators.
assertion.objects: The exact kernel on the full Tate module, all retained ring-class and quadratic fields; two evaluated cohomology classes; their finite localizations and original cochain basis matrices.
assertion.hypotheses: The fixed nontrivial scalar element survives the characteristic-zero test; actual evaluation is injective. The fixed matrix-span witness gives absolutely irreducible rank-two summands; moving scalar character is nonquadratic and conjugation exchanges summands. Finite quotient cochain data and finite Chebotarev are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For each such pair of independent classes and the specified finite-stage data, there is an actual kernel element and a compatible finite-stage prime/place.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero inner or outer fraction-field tests with nonquadratic moving character. Residual characteristic2 assertions are expressly weaker.
assertion.uniformity: The same inner ultrafilter gives exact matrix equality for each retained outer instance before its possibly varying denominators.
assertion.constants: No uniform denominator bound is assumed; only the existing bounded cohomology/detecting-list inputs are used.
assertion.normalizations: Kernel restriction uses the central scalar modulo the kernel, not an element inside it. Equality L_j=E_(sigma_j squared) is between original Lambda matrices before composition with I_j.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No residual irreducibility or residual rank-two localization is asserted. Quadratic height-one specializations require their separate proof. Chebotarev is used on actual finite composita, never on the product group. Long t-jets are not 2-adic approximations where t is a unit.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain the kernel element on the characteristic-zero test; place all original cochain/Tate/field data in one compatible finite compositum; choose prime and place; pass to exact inner matrix identity; only then apply minimal-model maps.
